title: Stability threshold heuristics — personal log
body:
Context and intent:
This is a personal scratchpad documenting my thinking about quantitative thresholds we can use during slow rollouts (canary -> ramp -> full). I want compact, operational heuristics that an on-call engineer can follow without diving into a long playbook. Keep it simple, conservative by default, but tunable per-customer and per-model.

Goals:
- Define minimum set of signals (latency, errors, quality regressions) and concrete acceptance windows.
- Provide numeric formulas to translate telemetry into an automated pass/fail decision.
- Capture edge-case notes for pinning and partial rollbacks (e.g., variant-level failures, token-level quality drop).

Assumptions:
- Baseline metrics are taken from the last stable release 7 days prior to rollout.
- We have per-route p50/p95/p99, 5xx error rate, and a quality score (eval set delta or user-flag ratio).
- We can measure token-level cost/throughput but those are secondary.

Signals to observe (ordered by priority):
1) p95 latency delta: relative change vs baseline. Use 95th percentile to capture tail behavior.
2) error rate ratio: current 5xxs / baseline 5xxs (if baseline 0, treat as absolute >0.1% threshold).
3) quality-drop-per-1k-requests: number of failing eval prompts per 1000 requests (or increases in user flags).
4) throughput / queue-length: sudden drop indicates backpressure.
5) client-level anomalies (abnormally high retry rate).

Threshold heuristics (operational defaults):
- p95 latency: PASS if (p95_current - p95_baseline) / p95_baseline <= 0.20 (i.e., <=20% increase). WARN if 20%-40%. FAIL if >40% or absolute p95 > 2s for latency-sensitive routes.
- 5xx error rate: PASS if error_rate_current <= max(2x baseline, 0.002). WARN if between 2x and 5x baseline. FAIL if >5x baseline or >1% absolute.
- quality regressions: PASS if delta_eval_rate <= 0.5 regressions per 1k requests. WARN at 0.5-2 per 1k. FAIL >2 per 1k.
- composite score: weighted sum (latency_score * 0.45) + (error_score * 0.35) + (quality_score * 0.2). Map to PASS/WARN/FAIL by cutoffs (<=0.4 PASS, 0.4-0.7 WARN, >0.7 FAIL). Keep weights simple and documentable.

Quick formulas (pseudocode):
- latency_score = clamp((p95_rel_delta / 0.5), 0, 1)  # 50% relative increase maps to score 1
- error_score = clamp((error_ratio - 1) / 4, 0, 1)    # 5x maps to 1
- quality_score = clamp((regs_per_1k / 2), 0, 1)      # 2 regs/1k maps to 1

Examples (numbers):
- Baseline p95 = 800ms, current p95 = 1.0s -> rel delta = 0.25 -> latency_score = 0.5 -> partial concern.
- Baseline 5xx = 0.02% -> current 5xx = 0.08% -> error_ratio = 4 -> error_score = (4-1)/4 = 0.75 -> bad.
- Eval regressions: 1.2 per 1k -> quality_score = 0.6.
Composite = 0.45*0.5 + 0.35*0.75 + 0.2*0.6 = 0.225 + 0.2625 + 0.12 = 0.6075 -> WARN.

Rollout checklist (for slow rollout owner):
- [ ] Set 7-day baseline snapshot (timestamp and IDs) and attach to rollout ticket.
- [ ] Configure telemetry queries and dashboard widgets (p95, 5xx, reg rate).
- [ ] Canary cohort: 0.5% of traffic for 30m, then 1% for 1h, then 5% for 3h (default cadence). Adjust for long-lived sessions.
- [ ] Wire composite-score alert: fail -> immediate 100% stop and rollback; warn -> hold at current fraction + page on-call if stays >10m.
- [ ] Document pinning plan: which clients can be pinned, duration (default 48h), and process to request extension.
- [ ] Note warmup traffic: synthetic or replayed requests if available for cold caches.

Pinning decision template (short):
- When to pin: repeated failures localized to small subset of clients or model variant causing regressions for a high-value cohort.
- Pin window: 48 hours by default; extend only with sign-off from SRE + product.
- Steps: identify affected clients -> create pin request (inc ticket key) -> apply pin config -> monitor for 2x baseline window.

Rollback criteria (fast-fail):
- Composite score > 0.8 for >5 minutes OR
- Absolute p95 > 3x baseline OR
- Error rate increase that causes customer-visible 5xxs > 0.5% OR
- Severe quality drop: >5 regs per 1k for 15m.

Telemetry queries I use frequently (placeholders):
- p95_rel_delta: SELECT p95_current, p95_baseline, (p95_current - p95_baseline)/p95_baseline FROM telemetry WHERE route = 'XXX' AND timestamp BETWEEN start AND end
- regs_per_1k: SELECT count(flagged)/ (requests/1000) FROM evaluations WHERE model = 'M' AND window = '30m'
Make sure to include rollout_id and baseline_snapshot in queries.

Experiment log (notes):
- 2025-09-03: ran small canary for model-v15 on /chat-completion -> 0.5% -> p95 +18%, 5xx unchanged, evals 0.7/1k -> composite 0.37 -> passed to 1%. Observed soft-failure when CPU was contended on host-12 (need host isolation check).
- 2025-09-05: 5% ramp at 3h produced p95 spikes coincident with cache-eviction events; mitigated by increasing KV cache TTL on that route. Made note to add cache-warm step before ramp to 5%.
- 2025-09-07: user-flag spike from edge region us-west2 tied to a downstream reranker change (not our model). Lesson: correlate downstream service metrics early.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Where to store final baseline snapshots for easy lookup? (confluence vs telemetry snapshots service) -> pref: snapshot service, but need retention policy.
- Should we bake default weights per product line? e.g., conversational vs search have different latency tolerances.
- Automate pin requests? Maybe a templated Slack flow for SRE approval.
- Run a rehearsal with SRE: simulate FAIL condition and practice emergency rollback.

Notes to self:
- Keep the composite score simple. Engineers on-call shouldn't need calculus to interpret it.
- When in doubt, fail closed for latency-sensitive routes.
- Document a short one-pager for on-call with exact commands to pin/rollback.

Next steps (short):
1) Draft a one-page checklist for the on-call playbook and sync with Jules.
2) Add example queries to the rollout ticket template.
3) Propose default weights for conversational/search in next eng sync (scheduled Sep 12).
